preconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 100000 and 0 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 100000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each missile's time (t_i) and frequency (f_i) are integers within the bounds 0 ≤ t_i, f_i ≤ 100000.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == N + 1 and all(int(stdin.splitlines()[i].split()[0]) <= int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1].split()[0]) for i in range(N))
preconditions.description: The first line is N (1 ≤ N ≤ 100000), followed by N lines of (t_i, f_i) sorted in non-decreasing order of t_i.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the minimum number of hackerX missiles required, bounded by 0 and N.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(stdout.strip()) <= len(set((t, f) for t, f in missiles)) + len(set(f for t, f in missiles)) for missiles in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])
postconditions.description: The output is the smallest integer k such that there exists a way to assign each missile to a hackerX missile (with tunable frequency) where no hackerX missile is assigned to more than one missile at any time t, and the time to retune between consecutive assignments for a hackerX missile does not exceed the time difference between their arrival times.
